literal: Now that the tasks of the three seasons are already attended to, the five teachings cultivated together, the army and columns already ordered, and the sacrificial vessels not neglected—is this not one who excels in both!
idiomatic: With the three seasons' work already in hand, the five teachings pursued together, the armies already in order, and the ritual vessels never neglected—is this not true excellence in both war and peace!

literal: Immediately allocate places for schools and calculate where to erect lecture halls.
idiomatic: He immediately set aside sites for schools and planned where to build lecture halls.

literal: The sons and younger relatives of lieutenants and generals were all ordered to enter school; the sons and younger relatives of my own house were likewise ordered to receive instruction.
idiomatic: The sons and younger kinsmen of staff officers and generals were all sent to school, and the younger men of his own household were ordered to study as well.

literal: From the four bureaus, those broadly learned, knowing principle, and versed in literature and statecraft—to establish a Libationer of the Confucian Forest with rank equal to the Three Offices and generous stipends; all were finely chosen men of the realm—there would surely be suitable ones to fill this office.
idiomatic: From the four ministries he chose men of broad learning, moral discernment, and literary and political skill to establish a Libationer of the Confucian Forest, with rank equal to the Three Offices and generous support. Only the finest scholars of the realm were to be selected; surely suitable men could be found for the post.

literal: Recently Linchuan and Linhe two commanderies both requested to repair and restore schools—the request may be approved and transmitted downward.
idiomatic: Recently both Linchuan and Linhe commanderies had asked to repair their schools; the request was approved and sent down.

literal: Those who are not of the tie-of-dried-meat stream, whom ritual teaching does not reach, yet who wish to use connections to evade corvée—shall not be enrolled as students.
idiomatic: Anyone outside the proper student body, beyond the reach of ritual instruction, who sought connections to escape labor service was not to be enrolled.

literal: Clearly establish regulations, making the law clear and human dignity prized.
idiomatic: Regulations were set out plainly so that the law would be clear and learning would be honored.

literal: Further, ritual vessels such as sacrificial stands and cups were prepared, for the great archery rite was to be performed.
idiomatic: Ritual vessels—stands, cups, and the like—were also made ready for the great archery ceremony.

literal: Liang soon died, and it was again abandoned.
idiomatic: Liang soon died, and the project was abandoned once more.

literal: In the ninth year of Emperor Xiaowu's Taixuan reign, the Master of Writing Xie Shi again submitted a memorial saying:
idiomatic: In the ninth year of Emperor Xiaowu's Taixuan reign, Master of Writing Xie Shi submitted another memorial:

literal: The Way of establishing humanity is called benevolence and righteousness.
idiomatic: The way to establish a human being is through benevolence and righteousness.

literal: To assist goodness and nurture character, nothing but ritual and learning.
idiomatic: To foster goodness and shape character, nothing serves better than ritual and learning.

literal: Though principle arises from nature, it must be guided and led.
idiomatic: Though principle is innate, it must still be cultivated and guided.

literal: Thus at Zhu and Si the wind of spreading the Dao was opened; in the Odes and Documents the canonical models of instruction were handed down.
idiomatic: That is why the stream of the Way flowed from Zhu and Si, and why the Odes and Documents handed down the canonical models of instruction.

literal: Honoring the Odes and taking joy in ritual—royal transformation thereby flourished;
idiomatic: Revering the Odes and delighting in ritual, royal transformation rose accordingly;

literal: Refining and molding the nine currents of learning, the multitude of lives thereby attained harmony.
idiomatic: and by refining every current of learning, the people were brought to harmony.

literal: Ages are not constantly well-ordered, and the Way likewise perishes at times.
idiomatic: The world is not always well governed, and the Way too is lost from time to time.

literal: Guangwu cast aside weapons and took up recitation; Weiwu rested his horses to cultivate learning—such was their fear of letting this culture fall away.
idiomatic: Emperor Guangwu laid down his weapons to study the classics; Cao Cao halted his campaigns to promote learning—such was their dread of letting civilization collapse.

literal: Great Jin received the Mandate, encountering a world of many obstacles; though sagely transformation daily deepened, the royal Way was not yet complete—the work of schools was sometimes abandoned, sometimes revived.
idiomatic: When Great Jin received the Mandate, the age was full of obstacles. Though sagely influence spread day by day, the royal Way was still incomplete, and the work of the schools was now abandoned, now revived.

literal: Thus the daily work of molding and casting was lacking; the people's nature received no benefit like silk from the cocoon; the thread of subtle learning lay buried and could not be drawn forth—this is why your servant, searching far in humble reflection, sighs ceaselessly waking and sleeping.
idiomatic: The daily work of moral shaping was left undone; the people gained none of the refining benefit of raw silk; the subtle thread of learning lay buried and could not be drawn out. That is why your servant, searching far in humble thought, sighs without rest, waking or sleeping.

literal: Now the imperial majesty shakes the distant quarters, the war-chariots have just stilled—we shall shower the subtle wind over the four quarters and guide this people to supreme virtue.
idiomatic: Now imperial majesty reaches the far corners, and the chariots of war have just stilled. It is time to spread the subtle wind across the realm and lead the people to supreme virtue.

literal: How can we not broadly spread ritual and music, making them splendid and visible to all?
idiomatic: How can ritual and music not be broadly restored, so that they shine forth for all to see?

literal: I beg to revive the National University, to instruct the crown prince's sons;
idiomatic: I beg that the National University be revived to instruct the sons of the nobility;

literal: Send orders to the provinces and commanderies, and broadly restore village schools.
idiomatic: and that orders be sent to the provinces and commanderies to restore local schools everywhere.

literal: Polishing jade and gems—matching treasures will surely arrive; opening wide the ignorant masses, making this cultivated virtue flourish.
idiomatic: Polish jade and gems, and matching treasures will come of themselves; open wide the untaught masses, and cultivated virtue will flourish.

literal: Without slackening in the task, if one must proceed through this to thoroughness, then people will compete in their studies, the Way will rise high, and learning will be complete.
idiomatic: If the work is pursued without slackening and carried through to completion, people will vie in their studies, the Way will rise high, and learning will be whole.

literal: Emperor Lie accepted his words.
idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu accepted his proposal.

literal: That year, sons of high ministers and two-thousand-shi officials were selected as students; one hundred fifty-five additional temple halls were built.
idiomatic: That year sons of high ministers and two-thousand-shi officials were chosen as students, and one hundred fifty-five new academy halls were built.

literal: But rank and evaluation lacked clear rules; gentlemen and nobles were ashamed to stand in their ranks.
idiomatic: Yet rank and evaluation had no clear standards, and gentlemen were ashamed to be counted among the students.

literal: The Libationer of the National University Yin Mao spoke of it, saying:
idiomatic: Yin Mao, Libationer of the National University, addressed the matter:

literal: Your servant has heard that spreading transformation and correcting custom depend on ritual teaching; assisting character and completing virtue require learning.
idiomatic: Your servant has heard that to spread transformation and set custom right one must rely on ritual instruction, and that character and virtue are completed only through learning.

literal: This is how the former kings molded the realm, bridged all things, barred evil and received goodness—quietly permeating daily life.
idiomatic: By this the former kings molded the realm, bridged all things, turned aside evil and received goodness, quietly suffusing daily life.

literal: Thus they could open and penetrate subtle principle, exhaust the recondite and minute, thread together past and present, and weave through governance and transformation.
idiomatic: Thus they could open subtle principle, exhaust the hidden and minute, thread past and present together, and weave governance and transformation into one whole.

literal: Moreover the Master praised Hui, taking love of learning as the root; at seventy, few could look up to him—through skillful guidance one returns to the source.
idiomatic: The Master praised Hui for loving learning above all else; at seventy, few could match him, for through skillful guidance one returns to the root.

literal: The tones of the Ya and Song hymns flow in song for a thousand years—the deep model of sages and worthies, the shared wind of wise kings.
idiomatic: The tones of the Ya and Song have flowed in song for a thousand years—the deep model of sages and worthies, the common wind of wise kings.

literal: Since the restoration of Great Jin, founding its base east of the Yangtze, it honored and clarified schools, constructed and repaired academies—sons of high ministers all entered the National University.
idiomatic: Since the restoration of Jin south of the Yangtze, schools were honored, academies built and repaired, and sons of high ministers all entered the National University.

literal: Soon many troubles arose, and instruction was not carried through to completion.
idiomatic: Soon troubles multiplied, and instruction was never carried through.

literal: Your Majesty, with sagely virtue mysterious and unified, thinking to elevate former excellence, accommodating and harmonizing with the directions, guiding and reaching the nature of things, has revived the halls of Confucian learning—all join with the younger generation.
idiomatic: Your Majesty, with unified sagely virtue, seeks to raise up former excellence, harmonizing with the directions and guiding the nature of things, and has revived the halls of Confucian learning so that all may join the younger generation.

literal: Since the schools were established, years have passed, yet there is no accomplishment to speak of.
idiomatic: Years have passed since the schools were founded, yet there is nothing to show for it.

literal: Fearful of studies, evading corvée—those who actually remain are few; some falsely claim parental illness—truth and pretense are hard to know; name and reality are utterly confused—nothing exceeds this.
idiomatic: Students shun their work and dodge service; few actually remain. Some falsely plead parental illness, and truth and pretense are hard to tell apart. Name and reality are utterly confused—nothing is worse.

literal: Your servant has heard the old system: National University students were all from distinguished clans and noble descent, ranked alongside the imperial heir's sons.
idiomatic: Your servant has heard that under the old system National University students were all from eminent clans and noble houses, ranked alongside the imperial heir's sons.

literal: But now orchid and mugwort are mixed together—so that public sentiment is ashamed of it.
idiomatic: Now orchid and mugwort are mixed together, and public sentiment is ashamed of the institution.

literal: When Zigong wanted to do away with the lamb offered at the new moon, Confucius still treasured the ritual—how much more when name and reality are both lost, and one faces a wall for a lifetime!
idiomatic: When Zigong wished to abolish the lamb offered at the new moon, Confucius still upheld the ritual—how much more when name and reality are both lost and one remains ignorant for a lifetime!

literal: If because of today's urgent troubles there is no leisure for this institution, and it is provisionally suspended—that is another matter.
idiomatic: If today's urgent troubles leave no room for this institution and it is provisionally suspended, that is another matter.

literal: If not so, one should follow the old standard.
idiomatic: If not, the old standard should be followed.

literal: Your servant privately holds that sons and nephews of ministers within and without, of clear official rank, should universally enter school, regulated by curriculum and examination.
idiomatic: Your servant privately holds that sons and nephews of officials within and without the court, from respectable official families, should all enter school under a fixed curriculum and examination system.

literal: As for present students, some are at an age of resistance, square and round in different inclinations—they should be allowed to stay or go, each following what suits him.
idiomatic: As for current students, some are at a stubborn age and differ widely in temperament; they should be allowed to stay or leave, each as he chooses.

literal: What I have submitted may be in error; I beg that it be sent out for external deliberation.
idiomatic: What I have submitted may be mistaken; I beg that it be referred for external deliberation.

literal: Emperor Lie issued an edict praising and accepting it, yet again it was not implemented.
idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu issued an edict praising and accepting the proposal, yet once again nothing was done.

literal: Throughout the court and among commoners with a mind for learning, none failed to swell with indignation and sigh.
idiomatic: Throughout the court and among commoners who cared for learning, none failed to burn with indignation and sigh.

literal: Li Liao of Qinghe submitted another memorial: "Your servant has heard that teaching is the root of governance and transformation, the beginning of human relations—it is how one leads and reaches the many directions, advances virtue and raises benevolence, like clay and stone, molded and fired into vessels.
idiomatic: Li Liao of Qinghe submitted another memorial: "Your servant has heard that teaching is the root of governance and the beginning of human relations—the means by which the many are guided, virtue advanced, and benevolence raised, like clay and stone shaped in the kiln into useful vessels.

literal: Though the hundred kings differ in ritual, substance and ornament vary—yet as to this Way, its use is unerring.
idiomatic: Though the hundred kings differed in ritual and substance and ornament varied, the use of this Way never failed.

literal: Since the Central Kingdom was submerged, Queli lay in ruins, the former kings' bounty slept, and the wind of sages and worthies was cut off—from then until now, it will soon be a hundred years.
idiomatic: Since the heartland fell, Queli lay in ruins, the grace of the former kings faded, and the wind of sages and worthies was cut off—from then until now nearly a hundred years have passed.

literal: Creation has spirit; after denial comes renewal—the Yellow and Ji rivers run clear, the sea and Mount Tai are open and unobstructed, the common people receive revival, and the duckweed and algae flourish in transformation.
idiomatic: Creation has its spirit: after long decline comes renewal. The Yellow and Ji rivers run clear, the sea and Mount Tai stand open, the people revive, and the realm stirs with new life.

literal: Yet the canonical instructions are not spread; the Ya and Song lie silent; the long-decayed custom's great ruin is not yet corrected.
idiomatic: Yet canonical instruction is not spread abroad; the Ya and Song lie silent; the deep corruption of long decay is not yet set right.

literal: Unless this culture is unfolded and these great designs gathered and made bright, how can one glorify and assist the harmony of the age and multiply the flourishing transformation?
idiomatic: Unless this culture is spread and these great designs gathered into light, how can the age be harmonized and flourishing transformation multiplied?

literal: There are matters that seem distant yet are urgent—this is what is meant.
idiomatic: Some matters seem remote yet are urgent—this is one of them.

literal: My deceased father, the former subject Hui, pacified and gathered the commandery and town, and returned in loyalty to this court.
idiomatic: My late father, the former subject Hui, pacified the commandery, gathered the people, and pledged loyalty to this court.

literal: In the tenth year of Taixuan, he sent your servant to submit a memorial.
idiomatic: In the tenth year of Taixuan he sent me to submit a memorial.

literal: Passing through Queli, I visited the Temple of Confucius; the courtyard and buildings had collapsed, the models and forms were decayed—the master craftsman of ten thousand generations had suddenly fallen into ruin. Looking up and down, I could not keep tears from flowing.
idiomatic: On the road I passed through Queli and visited the Temple of Confucius. The buildings had collapsed, the rites fallen into decay—the master craftsman of ten thousand generations lay suddenly in ruin. Gazing up and down, I wept without knowing it.

literal: Having reached the capital, I submitted a memorial requesting the revival of sacrifice to the Sage and the restoration of lectures and learning.
idiomatic: On reaching the capital I submitted a memorial asking that sacrifice to the Sage be revived and lectures and learning restored.

literal: On the seventeenth day of the eleventh month of the fourteenth year, I received a clear edict adopting your servant's humble proposal and ordering Yan Province and Lu Commandery to restore the buildings according to the old standard.
idiomatic: On the seventeenth day of the eleventh month of the fourteenth year I received an imperial edict adopting my humble proposal and ordering Yan Province and Lu Commandery to restore the buildings according to the old standard.

literal: The late Director of the Masters of Writing Xie Shi had the items your servant required listed and submitted; he also contributed cloth from his household as a modest aid to the undertaking.
idiomatic: The late Director of the Masters of Writing Xie Shi listed and submitted the supplies I required and also contributed household cloth as a modest contribution to the work.

literal: The late General Who Pacifies the North, Prince Qiao of Qiao, appointed your servant acting Magistrate of North Lu County and granted permission for supplies and transport.
idiomatic: The late General Who Pacifies the North, Prince Qiao of Qiao, appointed me acting magistrate of North Lu County and authorized supplies and transport.

literal: Both ministers died, and the established plan was not carried through.
idiomatic: Both ministers died, and the plan was never completed.

literal: Your Majesty embodies the literary thought of Tang of Yao, seeks the diligent skillful guidance of Confucius, pities the decay and obscurity of what survives in ruins, and grieves that sound instruction has not yet soaked the realm.
idiomatic: Your Majesty embodies the literary thought of Emperor Yao, seeks the diligent guidance of Confucius, pities the decay of what survives in ruins, and grieves that instruction has not yet reached every corner of the realm.

literal: Your servant humbly holds that the Inspector of Yan Province should again be ordered by imperial rescript to complete the old temple, exempt several households, and assign them to sweeping and sprinkling.
idiomatic: I humbly propose that the Inspector of Yan Province again be ordered by imperial rescript to complete the old temple, exempt several households, and assign them to its upkeep.

literal: Also grant the Six Classics, establish lectures and schools, invite veteran scholars, gather many younger students, and make them enter the Way as naturally as oil spreads—unleashing the work of cutting and polishing.
idiomatic: Grant the Six Classics, establish schools and lectures, invite veteran scholars, gather young students in numbers, and let them enter the Way as naturally as oil spreads—unleashing the work of cutting and polishing.

literal: Deploy benevolence and righteousness in campaigns, spread virtue to win the distant—what will not come when summoned, what will not submit when gently treated?
idiomatic: Wield benevolence and righteousness in war, spread virtue to win the distant—who would not come when called, who would not submit when treated with kindness?

literal: What is done is small; what is spread is great.
idiomatic: The deed itself is small; what it spreads is vast.

literal: Your servant, since coming to serve at the capital, has now been eight years; separation from parents has accumulated, and morning and night have brought no peace.
idiomatic: I myself have served at the capital for eight years now; separation from my parents has grown long, and day and night I have known no peace.

literal: General Who Strengthens the Military He Tanzhi now pacifies the three Qi regions; your servant should follow him on his return.
idiomatic: General Who Strengthens the Military He Tanzhi now pacifies the three Qi regions, and I should return with him.

literal: Turning back toward the capital, my gratitude and longing know no limit.
idiomatic: As I turn back toward the capital, my gratitude and longing know no bounds.

literal: I beg that your servant's memorial be sent out for external deliberation.
idiomatic: I beg that my memorial be referred for external deliberation.

literal: " Again it was not examined.
idiomatic: Again it was not examined.

literal: When the Founding Emperor of Song received the Mandate, he ordered the relevant offices to establish schools; before it was completed he died.
idiomatic: When the Founding Emperor of Song received the Mandate, he ordered the relevant offices to establish schools, but died before the work was finished.

literal: In the twentieth year of Emperor Wen's Yuanjia reign, the National University was restored; in the twenty-seventh year it was abolished.
idiomatic: In the twentieth year of Emperor Wen's Yuanjia reign the National University was restored; in the twenty-seventh year it was abolished.

literal: In the third year of Ganlu, during the reign of the Noble Township Lord of Wei, the imperial carriage personally led the assembled officials in performing the rite of nourishing the aged at the Imperial Academy.
idiomatic: In the third year of Ganlu, under the Noble Township Lord of Wei, the emperor personally led the assembled officials in performing the rite of nourishing the aged at the Imperial Academy.

literal: Thereupon Wang Xiang served as Elder of the Three, and Zheng Xiaotong as Fifth Watch.
idiomatic: Wang Xiang served as Elder of the Three, and Zheng Xiaotong as Fifth Watch.

literal: Today there is no commentary on this, yet the Han rites survive in full.
idiomatic: No commentary on this survives today, yet the Han rites remain fully recorded.

literal: In the twelfth month of the sixth year of Emperor Wu of Jin's Taishi reign, the emperor visited the Imperial Academy and performed the district drinking ceremony.
idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the sixth year of Jin Emperor Wu's Taishi reign, the emperor visited the Imperial Academy and performed the district drinking ceremony.

literal: The edict said: "Ritual and ceremony have long been abandoned; only now are the old canons again studied and practiced.
idiomatic: The edict read: "Ritual and ceremony have long lain in ruin; only now are the old canons again studied and practiced.

literal: Grant the Director of Ceremonies one hundred bolts of silk, and oxen and wine to the vice director, academicians, and students.
idiomatic: Grant the Director of Ceremonies one hundred bolts of silk, and oxen and wine to the vice director, academicians, and students.

literal: " In the third year of Xianning, and in the ninth year of Emperor Hui's Yuankang reign, the rite was again performed.
idiomatic: In the third year of Xianning and the ninth year of Emperor Hui's Yuankang reign, the rite was performed again.

literal: In the Zhengshi era under the Qi King of Wei, whenever the Qi King finished lecturing on the classics, he would have the Director of Ceremonies perform the libation to the former sages and former masters at the Imperial Academy—not in person.
idiomatic: In the Zhengshi era under the Qi King of Wei, whenever the king finished lecturing on the classics, he had the Director of Ceremonies perform the libation to the former sages and former masters at the Imperial Academy—he did not attend in person.

literal: When Emperors Hui and Ming were crown princes, and when Crown Prince Minhuai finished lecturing on the classics, each personally performed the libation at the Imperial Academy; the crown prince advanced in rank before the former master, and the Palace Companion advanced in rank before Yan Yuan.
idiomatic: When Emperors Hui and Ming were crown princes, and when Crown Prince Minhuai finished lecturing on the classics, each personally performed the libation at the Imperial Academy: the crown prince advanced in rank before the former master, and the Palace Companion before Yan Yuan.

literal: Emperor Yuan's edict said: "I remember when the crown prince did this—after the sacrifice he would invite princes and dukes and those below; in Luoyang we once shared quiet seats.
idiomatic: Emperor Yuan's edict said: "I remember when the crown prince did this—after the sacrifice he would invite the princes and dukes and those below; in Luoyang we once sat together in quiet audience.

literal: " Emperors Cheng, Mu, and Xiaowu likewise all personally performed the libation.
idiomatic: Emperors Cheng, Mu, and Xiaowu likewise all performed the libation in person.

literal: In Emperor Xiaowu's time, because the Imperial Academy south of the river was remote and suspended far away, the relevant offices proposed, following the first year of Shengping, to establish a provisional Imperial Academy at the central hall.
idiomatic: In Emperor Xiaowu's time, because the Imperial Academy south of the river was remote, the relevant offices proposed, following the first year of Shengping, to establish a provisional Imperial Academy in the central hall.

literal: At the time there were no longer National University students; the relevant offices memorialized: "One needs one hundred twenty students from the two schools.
idiomatic: At the time there were no longer National University students; the relevant offices memorialized: "One hundred twenty students from the two schools will be required.

literal: Take sixty Imperial Academy students from those presently enrolled; provisionally select sixty National University students from the sons and grandsons of great ministers; when the affair is finished, dismiss them.
idiomatic: Take sixty Imperial Academy students from those presently enrolled, and provisionally select sixty National University students from the sons and grandsons of great ministers; when the affair is finished, dismiss them.

literal: " The memorial was approved.
idiomatic: The memorial was approved.

literal: When the libation rite was finished, officials of the sixth rank and above were assembled.
idiomatic: When the libation rite was finished, officials of the sixth rank and above were assembled.

literal: In the twenty-second year of Yuanjia, the crown prince performed the libation, adopting the Jin precedent; the offices had their commentary.
idiomatic: In the twenty-second year of Yuanjia the crown prince performed the libation, following the Jin precedent; the offices had their commentary on the rite.

literal: When the sacrifice was finished, the Founding Emperor personally visited the academy banquet; the crown prince and all below attended.
idiomatic: When the sacrifice was finished, Emperor Wen personally attended the academy banquet; the crown prince and all below were present.

literal: Arms are the preparation for guarding the state.
idiomatic: Arms are what guard the state.

literal: Confucius said: "To lead the people to war without teaching them is to abandon them.
idiomatic: Confucius said: "To lead the people to war without teaching them is to throw them away.

literal: " Arms are an inauspicious affair; they cannot be set up in emptiness—one practices them through hunts and reviews.
idiomatic: War is an inauspicious affair and cannot be maintained in idleness; it is practiced through hunts and reviews.

literal: Whenever the army sets out it is called ordering the troops; when it enters it is called marshaling the columns—both are matters of battle formation, distinguishing the use of drums, bells, gongs, and cymbals, teaching the cadences of sitting, rising, advancing, retreating, fast and slow, sparse and dense—and thus the hunt field is used.
idiomatic: When an army sets out it is called ordering the troops; when it enters camp, marshaling the columns. Both concern battle formations: distinguishing the use of drums, bells, gongs, and cymbals, and teaching the cadences of sitting, rising, advancing, retreating, speed, spacing, and density—and so the hunt field serves as the school.

literal: The captured game is offered in sacrifice to the soil god.
idiomatic: The captured game is offered in sacrifice to the soil god.
